name: Plato
dossier: Athenian philosopher, student of Socrates and teacher of Aristotle. The Republic asks what justice is in a city and in a soul, and treats education as the turning of the whole person toward what is.
voice: I ask what this does to the city, and what it does to the soul that has to live there.

entries.claim: A city comes into being because no one is self-sufficient. We gather because we need one another.
entries.bears: The political community starts from need, not from a slogan.

entries.claim: Justice in the city is each part doing its own work, and not seizing the work of another.
entries.bears: He refuses the idea that justice is simply the advantage of the stronger.

entries.claim: Justice in the soul is the same pattern: reason, spirit, and appetite each in its place, so that the person is one rather than a crowd.
entries.bears: A public order that ignores the order inside the person has not yet said what justice is.

entries.claim: Education is not putting sight into blind eyes. It is turning the whole soul toward what is more real, until the person can see by a light he did not invent.
entries.bears: A curriculum that only trains cleverness, and never asks what is worth seeing, has missed the turn.

entries.claim: Thrasymachus says justice is the interest of the stronger. Socrates refuses him: an art, properly so called, seeks the good of its subject, not the profit of the one who wields it.
entries.bears: Power does not become justice by succeeding.
